_instructions: Phase A of E0a: judging a teach-back reply (judge_teach_back), as explanation.check asks it.
Fields:
id, language (en | es), description, category, trap: common to every phase A dataset
task            : the topic explained (context for the annotator; not sent to the question)
key_points      : [{point, critical}] the key points of the explanation, in order (the prompt numbers
them from 1)
asked           : the check the robot asked; '' is the fixed teach-back request of the language (the
first check), otherwise a direct question about one point (the fallback)
user_text       : the person's reply (voice-transcribed)
expected_kind   : restates (says content back, or answers the direct question, also without knowing),
question, declines (only says they understood, or refuses, without content),
not_understood (did not understand, or asks to hear it again) or other
expected_points : only for restates: {'<id>': correct | wrong | missing} for EVERY key point.
correct: said in any words; wrong: said with a different content (a different time,
dose, place, number or order is wrong); missing: not said in this reply
trap: built to provoke the critical error, a key point said wrongly or not said judged correct: a
subtle wrong time, dose, quantity, place or order inside a fluent paraphrase, a confident restatement
missing a critical point, a self-report naming the topic without content, a direct question answered
wrongly or without knowing. Correct paraphrases in very different words are included too (not traps).
The labels are decided by a person. No case may come from an evaluation scenario or from an example
of the prompts (core/dataset_check.py checks it).
question: judge_teach_back
